Check: Record the exact alert and intended destination
Evidence to capture: Customer; site; endpoint or service; monitor; alert ID; severity; state; first seen; last change; time zone; expected ticket destination
Common interpretation: An ambiguous alert identity prevents reliable downstream reconciliation
Safe next action: Freeze the original alert record and create a dated evidence copy
Escalation trigger: Alert identity or expected destination cannot be proven

Check: Capture the original route and delivery evidence
Evidence to capture: Route or policy version; suppression; maintenance; integration identity; attempt; response; retry; audit events
Common interpretation: A later configuration change can erase the conditions that caused the miss
Safe next action: Export or screenshot the original state before editing or replaying
Escalation trigger: Original evidence has expired or already been overwritten

Check: Search every plausible downstream location
Evidence to capture: Alert ID; device identity; customer; summary; correlation key; source; time window; unexpected; closed; merged; spam; unassigned queues
Common interpretation: The ticket may exist under an unexpected mapping or lifecycle state
Safe next action: Reconcile all matching records before replaying
Escalation trigger: A duplicate or partial ticket may already exist

Check: Define expected ticket behavior
Evidence to capture: Required fields; queue; owner; SLA; deduplication; recovery; stop condition; escalation owner
Common interpretation: Without a measurable contract there is no reliable pass or fail result
Safe next action: Write a bounded acceptance test and rollback before remediation
Escalation trigger: No owner or approved expected behavior exists

Check: Confirm the monitor produced the intended active alert
Evidence to capture: Threshold; samples; state transition; alert ID; active state; timestamps
Common interpretation: A warning or display state may never have been eligible for ticket creation
Safe next action: Prove the alert state transition before troubleshooting the connector
Escalation trigger: Monitor evaluation evidence conflicts with the displayed alert

Check: Verify route conditions matched at event time
Evidence to capture: Customer; site; device class; OS; tags; policy; severity; schedule; route version
Common interpretation: A valid alert can miss a route because one condition did not match
Safe next action: Compare recorded event values with the exact historical route conditions
Escalation trigger: Historical route conditions cannot be reconstructed

Check: Check suppression and lifecycle rules separately
Evidence to capture: Acknowledgement; suppression; maintenance; dependency; flapping; quiet hours; deduplication; recurrence; auto-resolution
Common interpretation: A designed suppression may explain no ticket but still require ownership and evidence
Safe next action: Confirm the exact rule and document whether the outcome was expected
Escalation trigger: Suppression hid an alert outside approved scope

Check: Compare affected and successful alerts
Evidence to capture: One affected alert; one success on same route; one unaffected event in same window; first differing condition
Common interpretation: The first difference usually narrows the fault to alert eligibility route or destination
Safe next action: Build a side-by-side evidence table and isolate one boundary
Escalation trigger: Failures span multiple customers routes or destinations

Check: Identify the selected route and its change history
Evidence to capture: Route ID; enabled state; priority; conditions; destination; integration version; configuration changes
Common interpretation: The alert may have selected no route or a different route than expected
Safe next action: Trace rule evaluation and preserve the selected route evidence
Escalation trigger: Route selection is unavailable or contradicts configuration

Check: Validate downstream field mappings
Evidence to capture: Customer; company; contact; site; queue; board; project; category; priority; status; assignee; SLA
Common interpretation: A stale or incomplete mapping can reject or misroute a ticket
Safe next action: Repair only the verified mapping and retest one canary
Escalation trigger: Customer or queue ownership is ambiguous

Check: Check required objects and field values
Evidence to capture: Retired objects; renamed queues; invalid custom fields; unsupported values; required-field changes; rejection detail
Common interpretation: A downstream schema or object change can break ticket creation without changing the alert
Safe next action: Update the narrow mapping or schema contract with approval
Escalation trigger: The downstream system changed requirements without a compatible route

Check: Validate integration identity and authorization
Evidence to capture: Credential or token ID; certificate; scopes; tenant; source IP policy; secret rotation; expiry; authentication logs
Common interpretation: Expired or under-scoped identity prevents creation even when the route is correct
Safe next action: Restore least-privilege authorization through the supported rotation path
Escalation trigger: Identity ownership is unknown or cross-tenant access is suspected

Check: Locate the outbound delivery record
Evidence to capture: Correlation ID; payload hash; attempt time; destination; redacted request; redacted response
Common interpretation: No record indicates failure before delivery or insufficient observability
Safe next action: Trace the last confirmed state without exposing secrets or customer data
Escalation trigger: No delivery evidence or correlation identifier exists

Check: Classify the delivery outcome
Evidence to capture: No attempt; client rejection; authentication; permission; validation; rate limit; timeout; server error; accepted but absent
Common interpretation: Different failure classes require different owners and retry decisions
Safe next action: Record the exact class and route it to the responsible system owner
Escalation trigger: A supposedly accepted request has no downstream record

Check: Review queue retry and deduplication state
Evidence to capture: Retry count; backoff; queue age; dead letter; ordering; concurrency; duplicate key; idempotency key; replay limit
Common interpretation: The request may be delayed dead-lettered or intentionally suppressed as a duplicate
Safe next action: Recover one bounded item through the documented queue path
Escalation trigger: Queue growth affects multiple customers or exceeds the recovery objective

Check: Correlate provider and downstream service evidence
Evidence to capture: Provider status; downstream status; application logs; audit logs; same time window; response body
Common interpretation: A generic HTTP success does not prove that a usable ticket was committed
Safe next action: Match both systems with one correlation chain and current status
Escalation trigger: Provider or downstream outage is active or historical evidence is missing

Check: Prove current downstream state before replay
Evidence to capture: Existing ticket; merged record; update; suppression; partial record; audit trail; correlation key
Common interpretation: Replaying without reconciliation can create duplicate work and pages
Safe next action: Record the current state and choose retry resume manual creation or no action
Escalation trigger: Partial or conflicting records already exist

Check: Correct only the verified defect
Evidence to capture: Actor; approval; time; prior value; new value; mapping or route; rollback
Common interpretation: A narrow change preserves causality and limits customer impact
Safe next action: Change one verified variable and retain rollback evidence
Escalation trigger: The fix requires broad routing or authorization changes

Check: Run one unique canary alert
Evidence to capture: Synthetic or approved target; unique correlation value; bounded destination; timeout; delivery evidence; duplicate search
Common interpretation: A canary proves the repaired path before broad replay
Safe next action: Test one controlled event and monitor the complete lifecycle
Escalation trigger: No safe test tenant target or destination is available

Check: Keep security and scope boundaries intact
Evidence to capture: Deduplication state; route scope; authentication; secret handling; retry limit; approvals
Common interpretation: Forcing a ticket by weakening controls creates a larger operational risk
Safe next action: Stop and escalate if the route cannot be repaired within approved boundaries
Escalation trigger: A proposed workaround disables controls or widens customer impact

Check: Verify one complete and correctly owned ticket
Evidence to capture: Ticket ID; customer; endpoint; queue; severity; summary; evidence; timestamps; owner; SLA; bidirectional link
Common interpretation: Creation is useful only if the ticket is correctly mapped and owned
Safe next action: Compare the result with the written acceptance contract
Escalation trigger: Ticket exists but ownership or customer mapping is wrong

Check: Test lifecycle transitions separately
Evidence to capture: Acknowledgement; assignment; escalation; recovery; update or closure; reopen; maintenance behavior
Common interpretation: Initial creation can pass while later operational states still fail
Safe next action: Run bounded tests for each required transition
Escalation trigger: Recovery or escalation behavior creates lost or duplicate work

Check: Reconcile the affected time window
Evidence to capture: Created; merged; expected suppression; failed; retried; dead-lettered; unknown; owned exception; totals
Common interpretation: A fixed canary does not resolve historical missed work
Safe next action: Assign every original event a final state owner and due date
Escalation trigger: Unknown or unowned outcomes remain after reconciliation

Check: Record prevention and closure evidence
Evidence to capture: Root cause; prevention; integration monitoring; residual risk; customer impact; owner; review date; evidence link
Common interpretation: Closure requires a durable control rather than a one-time green test
Safe next action: Approve the evidence pack and schedule monitoring and review
Escalation trigger: Root cause is unknown or prevention cannot be verified
